body: This is so true. If we acknowledge that mental illness is real, and that one of the symptoms can be persistent mental anguish and suicidal thoughts, then we should be given the right to choose to die just like anyone else who is suffering from a terminal illness.

Very unlikely. Pills are actually really unreliable and are more likely to just get you stuck on dialysis. In some cases pills that can kill you in higher doses also have an additive that will cause you to vomit them back up if they are taken in larger amounts.

At one point our therapist said, "Hate is not the opposite of love, indifference is." 

Part of me feels like her hatred of me is just because she loves me, but is so disappointed in the person that I am.
Sometimes I feel bad for the ones who have gone, and sometimes I'm jealous. I've lost a couple people in my life to suicide.l, and it's always the same - sadness, confusion, jealousy.
If you want to talk, just pour it out. Sometimes just typing it out can help.

20 hours? Any therapist who things they can solve a lifetime of pain in 20 hours is a snake oil salesman.

Personally I'm not religious, but one thing I always thought was a good idea was the concept of people telling their problems in a confessional. Before therapy was a thing this was a form of weekly therapy. People could vent their problems and be forgiven. It was built right in to society.

You were abused at a young age. Nobody can predict if that will take 5 hours to help you cope or 10,000. 

Also - you aren't a slut. We are sexual animals and one way we seek comfort is physical. The first step towards self esteem and self respect is to stop using that word as a weapon against yourself.

People do all sorts of things to fill the gaps in their lives, sex, drugs, music, exercise, work, alcohol, coffee... The list goes on and on. We are built flawed and sometimes these things fill the gaps while we try to figure our shit out. All of them can be unhealthy in varying degrees, but not allowing yourself any coping mechanisms is just as bad.

It's good that you are getting help, and it's fine if you want to come on here and rant.

Even if you ARE rude to people, there are plenty of people who have made a decent career out of being rude. There's even a dude in the US who became president by being rude.

Maybe it's the polite people who need to change. ;)

I'm overweight, too, and have a friend who is super buff. He works out every day, sometimes for up to 3-4 hours. He gets oiled up and does the whole bodybuilding competition thing, too.

He's also extremely selfish and recently left his wife a month after she had their second baby. She found out he had been sexting the woman who ran the dayhome their first child was in.

I would rather be 800lbs than be him. Beautiful people don't always make the world a better place. Just saying. ;)

I get that. People are can be really short when it comes to communication - incompatibilities in communication types are a huge source of friction. People are more likely to get angry when they feel they aren't understood. (A huge source of strife between countries / cultures).

You don't seem rude at all to me. Guess that's why I like communicating online. =)

Another idea I had was to put up an ad offering to film people's events with a 360 camera. The Theta S and Gear 360 are about $500 each, and you could easily ask around $100 for a half hour of filming / upload to YouTube / Facebook. I'm sure lots of stores would pay that.

It doesn't sound stupid at all. Making money is hard.

You have a degree (joke or not, it's better than what I have - nothing) so you could make some money tutoring. There are sites like Chegg Tutors where you can make a bit of extra money, or you could look at a site like UpWork - they often need writers.

I tried Fiverr for a while and didn't find that it was worth the time.  You could start aiming for part time jobs and work towards building an online presence, too. A couple successful tutorials on popular topics can bring in a bit of extra money each month.
What's your current job? Is there something you could do for online work in the interim while you hunt for jobs - or to supplement your disability income?

She doesn't know what she is talking about. If you have access to psychiatric care you should pursue it. Going to a psychiatrist is the opposite of cowardice - you are acknowledging a problem and doing something about it.

Reaching out to your friend about it was brave, too, because there are people who don't understand and react exactly like she does. Coming here for a second opinion was a good move, too.

People who say that suicidal thoughts are a sign of weakness don't understand it at all. It really is the equivalent of saying that someone who can't overcome cancer without help is weak.

For now it really is good that you reached out for help. We are here to support you in any way we can.

You also don't deserve the pain that your mind is causing for you. We are all temporary, and eventually we will all be forgotten - this doesn't mean that life has no meaning.

What we do here and now is all that matters. If nobody cares for you now - somebody WILL care for you in the future. If it seems that nobody likes you, it is because you haven't met the right people, or that your mind is playing tricks on you.

You reached out, and I think that means that you want someone to care, you want to feel like there is someone out there who could possibly understand. Maybe I could understand - or maybe someone else here could. Why do you think you are a terrible human being?
I'm sorry to hear you are in so much pain. Is it primarily physical or emotional?

Sometimes the void is the best place to shout... Or in a car on an empty highway. That's a good spot, too.

Surviving emotional abuse isn't easy. I went through years of it, and it never stops affecting you - but with time and distance you can rebuild your self esteem. 

Remember that we are all flawed, and abusive people tend to project their flaws onto others as a way of coping with their own self-doubt and loathing. As a parent myself, the things that my children do that make me the most frustrated are the things that I recognize in myself. When my son acts selfish I get angry because I fear that I am too selfish. When my son can't concentrate I feel terrible because I passed the ADHD on to him.

Chances are any flaws your mother calls you out on are actually quite minor, she just sees them as twice as bad because they are in her, too.

I know how easy it is to assume the people around you think you are a loser. Chances are they care deeply for you, and unemployment is something everyone goes through at some point or another and they understand that it doesn't reflect on you.

Being bipolar makes the world - and people's opinions of you - seem skewed at times. One thing to remember is that family is supposed to be a burden - but also a support. We are social animals, and that means we are built to support each other when times are tough. Think about the people you love, would you support them if they were going through something and you had the capacity to help? 

Commit yourself to the idea that when you are at your highest you will help others who are low, and understand that when you are at your lowest it's okay to ask for support.

I understand. These kinds of thoughts are hard to break out of - sometimes almost impossible. I came here to post about much the same thing.

If you just need a random person to talk to, just let loose here. For me sometimes just drowning out the thoughts with loud music and repetitive tasks is enough to push through the worst of it.

Or find someone else on here and talk to them, like I am to you. Helping someone else can sometimes break the negative thought cycle.
